messages:
jess-support: Customer reported repeated 504s hitting /v1/generate around 09:12 UTC during a traffic spike. They say it lasts ~30-90s then recovers. Escalating—link to customer logs: https://redwood.cust/4321 :face_with_thermometer:
noah-sre: thanks — can you paste a sample gateway log and the tenant id?
jess-support: tenant=acme-42. Gateway shows upstream 502/504s. Sample: `503 upstream read timeout from 10.23.5.12:8080`
noah-sre: initial hunch: scale-up lag. Did they hit any quota/rate-limit errors?
jess-support: no rate-limit in traces. Auth looked fine. Billing checks green.
oncall-bot: Incident created: #6298761234 - acme-42 timeout surge. Pager duty notified.
samir.eng: I see corresponding spikes in queue depth for the tenant. KEDA log shows poll loop delays. Poll interval 30s, cooldown 300s.
mira.ops: KEDA config for that tenant? Can you paste ScaledObject snippet?
samir.eng: sure:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: acme-42-scaled
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: inference-deployment
  minReplicaCount: 0
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  pollingInterval: 30
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prom:9090
      metricName: redwood_queue_len
      threshold: "50"
```
noah-sre: minReplicaCount=0 + cooldown 300s + polling 30s == potential long cold window. If model init is heavy, first request waits for pod readiness.
ryan-ml: model init logs from pod start show SDK loading and model shard init: `ModelLoader: INIT start` then `weights load complete` at ~22s, then `kvcache warmup 8s` — cold-start ~30s. That matches the customer window.
mira.ops: also noticed readinessProbe delays; readinessProbe has initialDelaySeconds: 5, timeoutSeconds: 1. Pod reported ready only after app-level init finished, so probe not shortening visible time.
samir.eng: KEDA sometimes misses rapid spikes if Prometheus scrape/alerting lags. Our scaledobject uses queue length metric that updates every 15s; combine that with pollingInterval 30s can be 45s+ to detect.
jess-support: customer said some requests got 504s even after scale-up started. Any fallback routing?
noah-sre: gateway routes to backend pool; when new pods are created there is a transient period before they pass readiness and get added. We should add a temporary fallback to a cheaper model variant to avoid 5xx.
ryan-ml: alternatives:
- set minReplicaCount to 1 or 2 for critical tenants
- reduce pollingInterval to 5s and cooldown to 60s for bursty customers
- add a prewarm job that keeps a hot instance with the model warmed
- enable KV cache snapshot restore to reduce warm time

mira.ops: repro steps I ran:
1) set minReplicaCount:0, pollingInterval:30, cooldown:300
2) generate synthetic spike of 800 qps for tenant acme-42 for 45s
3) observed first 18s: queue builds, next 30-60s: pods spin up but several requests timed out -> gateway 504s
logs:
```
[keda] ScaledObject: poll start
[keda] No scale needed
[k8s] Creating pod inference-deployment-7ffd
[k8s] Pod started at 09:12:23
[app] ModelLoader: INIT start
[app] ModelLoader: weights load complete (22s)
[gateway] 504 upstream timed out waiting for ready backend
```
noah-sre: actionable plan for prod:
- set minReplicaCount=1 for tenants with SLOs (temporary)
- apply patch to ScaledObject for pollingInterval=10 and cooldownPeriod=60 for bursty class
- add a routing fallback to smaller model in gateway policy
- ops: run a canary to verify no surge in infra cost
samir.eng: I'll prepare a rollout: patch acme-42 scaledobject to pollingInterval=10,cooldown=60 and update autoscaleClass=burst in our config map. Also enable an annotation `redwood.io/warmup: "true"` to keep a small warm cache for model inference.
jess-support: communicated plan to customer, asked for permission to change minReplicaCount on their tenant. They approved temporary minReplicaCount=1.
oncall-bot: Deployment note: patch applied to acme-42 scaledobject at 09:45 UTC by samir.eng
ryan-ml: after patching pollingInterval=10 and minReplicaCount=1 I re-ran the spike test. Result: cold-start 22s but no 504s because gateway routed to existing warm pod. Queue depth peaked but requests were served.
mira.ops: follow-ups: create a runbook entry for "bursty tenant scale-up" with checklist: minReplica guard, patched polling, fallback routing, warmup annotation. Add monitoring alert for queue growth > 40 sustained for 20s and slow rollup of node pod readiness > 15s.
noah-sre: we should also evaluate using HPA with custom metrics alongside KEDA for faster horizontal autoscaling in some clusters. KEDA is good but its poll cadence creates detection holes.
samir.eng: noted. I'll open a Jira to prototype HPA+Prometheus adapter for queue metric and test race conditions with KEDA.
jess-support: closing loop with customer — they confirm no repeat 504s during subsequent spike and appreciate quick turnaround :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident resolved and archived.
